package_info.package_name: Popup Builder WordPress plugin (malicious Custom JS injection)
package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all vulnerable versions with stored XSS flaw)
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers exploit a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject arbitrary JavaScript into the Custom JS or CSS sections. This allows malicious code to be stored in the WordPress database and executed in the browsers of site visitors, leading to unauthorized redirections, credential theft, and malware delivery.

execution_context.trigger: When a user visits a page containing a popup with injected Custom JS
execution_context.file_location: Popup Builder plugin's Custom JS section (stored in WordPress database, rendered in page HTML)
required_permissions: Network access (to perform redirection and exfiltration)
Ability to execute JavaScript in the user's browser

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At page load, the code executes in the user's browser, reads the user's cookies via document.cookie, and redirects the browser to a malicious external domain, resulting in cookie exfiltration and potential further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code reads sensitive user cookies and performs an unsolicited redirect to an external, attacker-controlled domain. This is a hallmark of malicious XSS payloads designed to steal session data or deliver additional malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Custom JS in a WordPress plugin should only enhance site functionality and never access sensitive user data or redirect users to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirects may occur for authentication flows or user navigation, but never with user cookies appended to third-party URLs or without user interaction.
key_indicators: Direct access to document.cookie in injected JavaScript
window.location assignment to a non-whitelisted, external domain
Presence of <script> tags in Custom JS/CSS fields
Redirection URL containing user cookie data

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits a stored XSS vulnerability in the Popup Builder plugin to inject malicious JavaScript into the Custom JS section.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is stored in the WordPress database and rendered on site pages.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits an infected page, the malicious JavaScript executes in their browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: The user's browser executes the injected code, resulting in redirection to a malicious domain with user cookies appended.

attack_chain.action: The malicious domain receives the user's cookies and may deliver further malware or attempt credential theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: exfiltration of session data, credential theft, or further exploitation of the user.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of <script> tags in Custom JS/CSS fields of WordPress plugins
Injected JavaScript that accesses document.cookie and transmits it to external domains
Unsolicited window.location redirects to non-whitelisted or suspicious domains
Redirection URLs containing user cookie data
file_indicators: Custom JS/CSS fields in Popup Builder plugin containing <script> tags
Unexpected or unauthorized modifications to wp_options or plugin-specific database tables (e.g., entries containing script tags or suspicious JavaScript code)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests or redirects to domains not associated with the legitimate site, especially those containing user cookie data in the URL
Redirections to known malicious or newly registered domains observed in site traffic logs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Regularly scan the contents of Custom JS/CSS fields in WordPress plugins for script tags or suspicious JavaScript patterns, such as access to document.cookie or window.location assignments to external domains. Use web application firewalls (WAF) to block or alert on outbound requests containing user cookies or unsolicited redirects. Monitor site pages for injected scripts and audit plugin configuration and database entries for unauthorized changes. Correlate network logs for unexpected redirections or data exfiltration attempts.
